title: Example 20-8: Primary and Secondary Stress

illustrates.quote: Syllable Stress Using Print Symbols. Different print signs may be used either before or after syllables to indicate stress. (See UEB, §15.2, Stress, for braille stress symbols.)

blocks.features: Prime marks after 'ar' (heavier, primary stress) and after 'mat' (lighter, secondary stress), the second followed by a space before 'ik'; schwa; parentheses

printCorrections.evidence: references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf p.542 (PDF page 542), rendered at 300 dpi and cropped to the Example 20-8 box: the print reads "(ar′ə mat′ ik)" - a clear word space follows the second prime, before "ik". The braille has a space at the same place (mat^.2 ik). The two primes differ in weight in print (first heavier, second lighter); the text keeps one U+2032 for both because the prime cannot say which is which - builder must learn that primary/secondary stress needs distinct characters (the runner still emits 7 for a prime). The space between the first prime and the schwa is not clear in the image, so it was left as it was.
